summary: Larry Hasson, tax partner at Ottawa accounting firm McIntyre & Associates and co-founder of the tax-payment fintech Remitian, walks David DiNardo through how he coaches new business owners to budget for sales tax, income tax and installments so they are never blindsided by a tax bill. He then explains how a nagging problem with his own clients (and his physician wife) missing CRA payments grew from a proof-of-concept tool inside his firm into a venture-backed startup now regulated in Canada and the US, led by MindBridge founder Solon Angel as CEO. The conversation covers controlled growth, when to incorporate, expanding into the States, and why Canadian founders tend to think too small.
takeaways: Larry's rule for new self-employed clients: money that flows into the business account is not yours until HST, income tax and next year's installments are set aside; transfer a budgeted amount to personal and leave the rest behind.

Year two is the cash crunch, because you pay last year's income tax, HST, and start quarterly installments for the current year all at once, which is why owners feel like their tax rate is 80 to 90 percent.

Missing an installment is expensive money: CRA charged roughly 10 percent interest last year (about 8 percent now, Larry's number), it is not deductible, and a missed payroll remittance can trigger a 10 percent penalty in a single day.

Incorporating is not automatically the right move; Larry builds a three-to-five-year plan first, and clients with personal goals like buying a house may stay unincorporated for years to use RRSP, TFSA and FHSA incentives.

Remitian was validated in layers: first with Larry's wife as the only customer, then across McIntyre's clients, then with partner firms ZenBooks and Crowe Soberman, always charging for the tool to prove it was real.

The startup only became a real business in late 2023 when Solon Angel pushed Larry to 'rightsize' the opportunity, raise capital, and target an enterprise firm rather than four-partner shops paying $15 to $20K a year.
Larry's lightning-round advice: the one number to watch weekly is cash flow, the biggest CRA red flag is unreconciled HST and payroll, and the sticky note on his first laptop would say 'email less'.
